title: Adrenaline, noradrenaline, isoprenaline, dobutamine, phenylephrine and salbutamol compared
ariaLabel: Schematic of what sympathomimetic drugs do through alpha-1, beta-1 and beta-2 receptors: alpha-1 narrows vessels and raises pressure, beta-1 raises heart rate and force, and beta-2 widens airway and muscle vessels. Adrenaline acts on all three, noradrenaline mostly on alpha-1 and beta-1, isoprenaline on beta-1 and beta-2, phenylephrine on alpha-1, dobutamine on beta-1, and salbutamol on beta-2.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.

nodes.label: Beta-1 signal
nodes.info: Receptors on heart cells that respond to adrenaline, noradrenaline, isoprenaline and dobutamine.

nodes.label: Alpha-1 signal
nodes.info: Receptors on vessel muscle that respond to noradrenaline, adrenaline and phenylephrine.

nodes.label: Beta-2 signal
nodes.info: Beta-2 receptors on muscle vessels, which widen them.

nodes.label: Heart rate and force
nodes.info: A teaching score for heart rate and force. Beta-1 stimulation raises it; a rise in pressure slows it through the baroreceptor reflex.

nodes.label: Blood pressure
nodes.info: A teaching score for blood pressure from vessel tone and heart output.

nodes.label: Airway width
nodes.info: A teaching score for airway width.

edges.label: beta-1 receptor
edges.info: Beta-1 agonists raise heart rate and force. Isoprenaline and dobutamine are mainly beta-1 and beta-2; adrenaline acts on alpha and beta receptors.
More heart stimulation raises heart rate and force.

edges.label: alpha-1 receptor
edges.info: Alpha-1 agonists (phenylephrine, noradrenaline, adrenaline) narrow vessels and raise pressure.

edges.label: beta-2 vessel effect
edges.info: Beta-2 stimulation (isoprenaline, adrenaline at low levels) widens vessels in muscle and can lower diastolic pressure.

edges.label: beta-2 receptor
edges.info: Beta-2 agonists (salbutamol, terbutaline, adrenaline, isoprenaline) relax airway muscle and widen the airway.

edges.label: reflex
edges.info: A rise in pressure triggers the baroreceptor reflex, which slows the heart. This is why phenylephrine and noradrenaline can slow the pulse.

edges.label: cardiac output
edges.info: A faster, stronger heart raises pressure.

sources: Where each class acts. Adrenaline acts on alpha-1, beta-1 and beta-2, noradrenaline mostly alpha-1 and beta-1, isoprenaline beta-1 and beta-2, phenylephrine alpha-1, dobutamine beta-1, and salbutamol beta-2. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Dopamine and its dose-related effects, ephedrine and indirect agents, amphetamines, dose and route, tachyphylaxis, extravasation injury, arrhythmia risk, use in shock, anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest protocols, and alpha-2 and beta-3 effects are left out. Heart, pressure and airway are teaching scores. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
